english.title: Political party - fail to deliver account pre-period end

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: POLITICAL PARTIES ELECTIONS AND REFERENDUMS ACT 2000

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the treasurer of a registered party, namely **(..SPECIFY PARTY..), immediately before the end of a relevant period, failed to deliver to the Commission under Section 45 of the Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000,

(A)_[a statement of accounts]_
(B)_[a notification]_
(C)_[an auditor's report]_

before the end of the said relevant period
english.legislation: Contrary to section 47(1)(b) of and Schedule 20 to the Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See Section 47(4) for "relevant period".
(ii) See Section 47(2) and (3) for defences.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
